children: Canada's main stock index climbed to a more-than-one-month high on Friday, led by gains in materials and energy shares, while investors assessed Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem's warning on persistent energy-price pressures on interest rates.
rose 0.8% to 36,406.48 points at 10:30 a.m. ET, its highest level since September 4. It was on track for a second consecutive weekly gain.
advanced 1% after prices of gold and silver rose
Brent crude fell 0.4% but remained above $100 a barrel, keeping attention on the energy sector
, which rose 1.2% on Friday and is up more than 60% so far this year

Strength in commodity-linked shares helped lift the resource-heavy Canadian benchmark after a sharp, AI-driven technology selloff rattled global markets earlier this week, with a more limited impact on the TSX

"Materials, gold in particular, and copper, we're pretty bullish on those materials sectors. That could help TSX go higher," said Michael Dehal, a senior portfolio manager at Dehal Investment Partners at Raymond James
Dehal said the index would be particularly sensitive to developments in the Middle East and movements in bond yields
Macklem said Canada has not raised interest rates yet but the longer elevated energy prices go on "the harder that gets"

The BoC is not expected to raise interest rates at its next monetary policy decision announcement on October 28, but money markets are pricing in a rate hike of 25 basis points in December, according to data compiled by LSEG
Data on the day showed that Canadian home sales extended their decline in September, after a drop in August, as higher mortgage rates and expectations of a rate hike weighed on demand
The consumer discretionary sector (.GSPTTCD) climbed 0.8%, led by Aritzia
rising 1.2% after Scotiabank resumed coverage with a 'sector outperform' rating
